items.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013
items.q: And a little trumpet player, her name was Jody White... So I added two notes... She walked through “Day by Day,” fine.

ctx.x: Is it hard to teach piano players and guitarists especially, what to do in a big band?

Yes. It really is. A lot of them get so locked on with a part, and we have no jazz piano instructors at Fredonia. The piano studio cannot interpret chords. So I’m trying to do that, even though I’m not a piano player. Even with a gun to my head I’m not a piano player. But I can voice and I can use the keyboard as a writing thing. But as far as comping, piano players don’t know how to comp. They think they have to play everything all the time. And I remember a clinic that Thad Jones did, somebody asked him,…

that rhythm. She walked through “Day by Day,” fine. Just absolutely fine. And I said, “all you have to do, when this chord comes up, you have to move it from a C down a step to a B flat, and it will sound just fine.” And it was great. Light bulbs were going on in people’s heads. And it was something like I’d used before but pretty much for myself.
